summary: Retire Pass C: parallels become a derived table (concept co-expression x thin scorer)
description:
Owner decision 2026-08-13: the PARALLELS leg (Pass C LLM pair classification) is measurable GPU cost for net-null benefit — replace it with a derived table. Same edges table shape, new tiny brain: the distilled (query,chunk) scorer grades every chunk against each of its accepted concepts once (~38k scores, ~8 min on GPU per corpus version), and a chunk's partners are the best-graded cross-tradition co-expressors of its concepts. No edge curation needed — the tags are vetted upstream; curation pressure moves to tags and taxonomy where the apply gate already sits.

Evidence + design record: rellm docs/edges/derived-parallels-proposal.md (cost table, 21/24 judged-good partner recovery, losses); prototype rellm tools/derived_parallels.py; snapshot trial verified 2026-08-13 — reader-panel SQL unchanged, panels render with via annotations, all 258 per-work golden assertions + 13/14 legacy gate pass identically (the one failure is pre-existing v50 drift, guru-web todo:e7b40dd5).

Standing constraints: prod untouched by agents (corpus push is the owner's); guru main protected — PR flow; model artifact is rellm runs/edges/scorer/2026-08-13-run1/student-3a2 (22.7M).

Ritual after migration: corpus update → per-work golden queries (guru-web ritual) → re-distill student (rellm scorer pipeline, ~1 GPU-hour scripted) → re-derive parallels. Known losses accepted: taxonomy-blind parallels, CONTRASTS as a pipeline (112 rows become curated/frozen).
